div.span: started as a gaming fair volunteer. built a product instead.
my dad wanted to control the hot tub on his phone. so i built it.
always building something
i built a dev dashboard because i didn't like my other dev dashboards
home lab is getting out of hand. good.
happiest when there's solder in the air
i have too many open tabs and half-finished PCBs
i think about edge cases in the shower
e-ink, deep sleep, wake stubs - this is my happy place
added one more feature. and then one more. and then one more.
C++ in the morning. TypeScript at night.
the LED blinks. we ship it.
got tired of spreadsheets at gaming fairs
i volunteer at things and accidentally ship software
if something annoyed me once, i'll fix it so it never does again
it compiles. mostly.
once saw a problem at an event. now it's a SaaS.
i automate things i could just do manually. it's a gift.
if it's broken, i'm already fixing it
built in NRW, shipped to the world
streams are live. overlays are custom. send help.
works on my machine. also works on the server. rare.
i care about the details nobody will notice
ADA manages my printer, spotify, and smart home. she's fine.
i speak microcontroller and server fluently
debugging is just detective work with worse coffee
i told myself i'd keep it simple this time
the PCB is fine. probably.
closed laptop. opened it again. just one more thing.
i built a stream deck plugin that deploys my own SaaS
yes it has a web portal. no i don't know why.
yes those OBS scenes have custom animated backgrounds. i made them.
building an open-source robot arm. currently in pieces.
it's 2am and the firmware finally deep-sleeps correctly
i have more projects than hours in the day. working on both.
